title: The Standard of Code Review
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Approve a change once it clearly improves overall code health even if imperfect; technical facts and data overrule opinions; the style guide is the authority on style; mark optional comments as Nit.

title: Small CLs
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Benefits of small changes; about 100 lines usually reasonable and 1,000 usually too large, reviewer decides; separate refactorings from feature work; include tests.

title: What to look for in a code review
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Review design, functionality, complexity, tests, naming, comments, style, consistency, documentation, every line and context, and point out good things.

title: Conventional Comments
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Comment labels (praise, nitpick, suggestion, issue, todo, question, thought, chore, note) and decorations (blocking, non-blocking, if-minor).

title: Refactoring
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Refactoring changes internal structure without changing external behaviour through small behaviour-preserving steps; second edition uses JavaScript examples.

title: Strangler Fig
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Replace legacy systems gradually by growing a new system alongside, using seams and transitional architecture, rather than a big-bang rewrite; article dated 22 August 2024.

title: Characterization Testing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Characterization tests document a system's actual behaviour, not its intended behaviour, by recording what the code produces; post dated 8 August 2016.

title: The Debugging Book: Introduction to Debugging
publisher: Andreas Zeller, CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Debugging as the scientific method: hypothesis, prediction, experiment, observation, refinement until a diagnosis; page changed 15 October 2024.

title: git-bisect documentation
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Binary search between good and bad commits; git bisect run exit codes: 0 good, 1 to 127 except 125 bad, 125 skip.

title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
supports: Opened with WebFetch. MAJOR for incompatible API changes, MINOR for compatible features, PATCH for compatible fixes; 0.y.z is initial development with no stability promise.

title: Node.js Release Working Group: release schedule
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Node 20 end of life 30 April 2026; Node 22 maintenance to 30 April 2027; Node 24 to 30 April 2028; Node 26 active LTS, end of life 30 April 2029; from Node 27 one release line a year with an alpha phase and every line promoted to LTS.

title: Status of Python versions
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Python 3.9 end of life 31 October 2025; 3.10 end of life 1 October 2026; 3.15 first released 9 October 2026; support windows for 3.11 to 3.15.

title: Supported Versions
supports: Opened with WebFetch. PHP 8.2 security fixes until 31 December 2026; 8.3 until 31 December 2027; 8.4 until 31 December 2028; 8.5 until 31 December 2029; two years active plus two years security support.

title: Release Notes, Laravel 13.x
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Support policy of 18 months bug fixes and 2 years security fixes; Laravel 13 released 17 March 2026 requiring PHP 8.3; Laravel 12 bug fixes until 13 August 2026 and security until 24 February 2027.

title: DORA's software delivery performance metrics
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Five metrics: change lead time, deployment frequency, failed deployment recovery time (throughput), change fail rate, deployment rework rate (instability); advice against comparing very different teams; updated 5 January 2026.

title: State of AI-assisted Software Development 2025
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The 2025 DORA report describes AI as an amplifier of an organisation's existing strengths and weaknesses; companion DORA AI Capabilities Model.

title: OWASP Top 10:2025
supports: Opened with WebFetch (owasp.org/Top10/2025 redirects here). A01 Broken Access Control through A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions, with A03 Software Supply Chain Failures and A05 Injection.

title: Regular expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Evil patterns have a repeated group containing repetition or overlapping alternation, such as (a+)+$; never build a regex from user input.

title: Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2, 2019
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A WAF rule regex caused catastrophic backtracking and CPU exhaustion, about 27 minutes of errors; remediation included staged rollouts, rule performance tests and a planned move to a regex engine with run-time guarantees.

title: SEC Charges Knight Capital With Violations of Market Access Rule
supports: Opened with WebFetch. On 1 August 2012 a defective, unused function and an incorrect deployment led Knight's router to send more than 4 million orders in 45 minutes and lose more than $460 million; inadequate deployment and testing controls; $12 million penalty announced 16 October 2013.

title: Upgrading GitHub from Rails 3.2 to 5.2
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The upgrade took about a year and a half; dual booting with two lockfiles let the team deploy continuously; one minor version at a time; lessons on upgrading early and incrementally; posted 28 September 2018.

title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Randomised trial with 16 developers and 246 issues: tasks took 19% longer with AI allowed, while developers believed they were faster; authors' caveats; page now marks results as outdated.

title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Late-2025 estimates of -18% and -4% task time (faster) with confidence intervals including zero; selection effects; METR calls it very weak evidence and is changing its study design.

title: 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey: AI
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 84% use or plan to use AI tools; 46% distrust versus 33% trust AI accuracy; 66% cite answers that are almost right but not quite as the top frustration.

title: About protected branches
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Required approving reviews, dismissal of stale approvals, code owner review, required status checks, push restrictions; rulesets as an alternative.

title: SP 800-218, Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1
publisher: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. SSDF version 1.1, published February 2022, a core set of high-level secure software development practices.

title: Software Security Code of Practice
publisher: GOV.UK (DSIT and DCMS, with the NCSC)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A voluntary code with 14 principles for software vendors, first published 7 May 2025, updated 15 January 2026.

title: Cyber Resilience Act
publisher: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Entered into force 10 December 2024; reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026; main obligations from 11 December 2027; covers manufacturers of products with digital elements, including software.

title: re: Regular expression operations
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Named groups as (?P<name>...); atomic groups and possessive quantifiers added in 3.11; re.fullmatch; re.VERBOSE; raw strings.

title: Regular expressions (JavaScript Guide)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. JavaScript flags d, g, i, m, s, u, v and y; named groups (?<Name>x); lookbehind assertions.
